```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Small pre-treatment predictive distance can coexist with a large
post-treatment evaluation difference. This issue is distinct from temporal
propagation of boundary error.

```{r}
library(TRSC)
g <- trsc_geometry(matrix(c(0, 1e-5), 1, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"))))
x <- c(A = 0, B = 1)
trsc_profile_distance(g, c(A = 1, B = 0), c(A = 0, B = 1))
trsc_deployment_modulus(g, x, epsilon = 1e-5)
```

The modulus maximizes evaluation difference over two simplex representatives
within the stated predictive radius. Its certified upper enclosure is not
itself a universal minimax lower bound: that interpretation requires admissible
two-point statistical experiments in the maintained model class.

```{r}
null <- trsc_geometry(matrix(c(0, 0), 1, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"))))
trsc_deployment_modulus(null, x, epsilon = 0)
trsc_evaluation_set(null, x, representative = c(A = 1, B = 0))
```

At radius zero there is exact evaluation ambiguity. More calibration cannot
remove a truly population-null fiber. Near-null directions instead create
statistical instability. TRSC retains them; it does not remove weak directions
through rank truncation to manufacture narrower intervals.

Numerical enclosures may also be conservative when the optimizer is inaccurate.
Inspect status, corrected dual bound and any certified gap separately from the
scientific width.
